COMMON API REFERENCE:
Blender 5.2.2 API facts, verified in a separate disposable Blender process:
- A mesh scene object is a bpy.types.Object with type 'MESH'; obj.data is its bpy.types.Mesh datablock.
- Vertex groups belong to obj.vertex_groups. Mesh datablocks (obj.data) have no vertex_groups attribute.
- VertexGroup.weight(index) is a method taking an integer vertex index. Do not use weight[index], weights[index], or pass a MeshVertex object.
- VertexGroup.add(index_sequence, weight, type) writes weights; use a sequence of integer indices and the 'REPLACE' mode for setting a value. Do not assign through .weight or invent a .weights array.
- Iterate obj.data.vertices once; each vertex has an integer .index. MeshVertex.groups holds assignment elements with numeric .group indices and .weight values; it does not support group-name membership lookups. Group-name lookup is available on obj.vertex_groups.
- Preserve source mesh data, UVs, weights, all shape keys, original materials and the existing rig. The host saves your derivative; solve(scene) must not call file-saving operators.
- Python's built-in len(sequence_or_collection) returns its number of elements; for example, len(array) or len(vector).
- MeshVertex.groups is a sparse collection of assignments. An assignment position is not a global vertex-group ID. Never use v.groups[group_index] to locate a group's weight. Match each assignment's .group against the desired VertexGroup.index, or use VertexGroup.weight(v.index) while handling missing membership as zero.
- Vertex IDs and group IDs are different: v.index identifies a vertex; group.index identifies a named vertex group. Each entry a in v.groups is an assignment object with group ID a.group and weight a.weight. To check membership, compare a.group with group.index, for example any(a.group == group.index for a in v.groups). Read a.group and a.weight as attributes; assignment objects are not (group_id, weight) tuples. Do not test integer membership with in on Blender collections or VertexGroup objects.
